headline: Shipment growth and pricing lift a sharp profit rebound
summary_short: Saia's Q2 2026 operating revenue rose 17.1% y/y to $956.5 million on 4.4% higher LTL shipments, 8.4% higher tonnage, and pricing gains, while diluted EPS jumped to $3.51 from $2.67 a year earlier as the operating ratio improved to 86.9% from 87.8%.
summary_long: Revenue growth came from higher fuel surcharge revenue (22.3% of revenue vs 14.6%, on higher diesel prices), 4.4% higher LTL shipments per workday, and 1.5% higher LTL revenue per shipment ex-fuel. Operating income rose to $125.2M from $99.4M as revenue growth outpaced cost increases: salaries/wages/benefits +$43.4M (volumes, ~3% wage increase, higher health costs), purchased transportation +$27.3M, fuel/opex/supplies +$37.1M. Net income was $94.3M ($3.51 diluted EPS) vs $71.4M ($2.67). YTD operating cash flow was $291.2M vs $279.8M; YTD net capex was $158.0M, down from $384.0M, with FY2026 net capex guided to $350-400M. A 7.1% general rate increase took effect July 6, 2026 on ~25% of revenue, and a ~3% wage increase took effect July 1, 2026.

drivers.explanation: Higher fuel surcharge revenue (from higher diesel prices), shipment volume growth, and pricing actions lifted revenue faster than cost growth, expanding operating margin.
17.1% y/y growth from higher fuel surcharge revenue, a 4.4% increase in LTL shipments per workday, and a 1.5% increase in LTL revenue per shipment excluding fuel surcharge.
Increased revenue was partially offset by higher compensation levels, increased fuel costs and increased purchased transportation expense.
Followed the operating income improvement; effective tax rate was roughly flat at 24.9% vs 25.3% a year earlier, and interest expense was lower on lower average borrowings.
Revolving Credit Facility had no outstanding borrowings at quarter-end after repayments during the period; $100M remains outstanding under the Private Shelf Agreement.
